findings.claim: The Fast pacing model counts all mapped topic pages against 120 minutes but does not preserve the frozen Fast-day learning route. FT9 assigns 108 minutes of pages, leaving 12 minutes for blocks that include a 15-minute diagnostic, a 70-minute direct project, a 15-minute timed task, warm-up, skim, and reflection. A passing day-total check therefore would not establish a teachable Fast route.

findings.claim: The blueprint applies S19’s 45-minute Review-block duration and a 15/30-minute learner schedule to FT11, although the frozen Fast day has no module-check block and its six blocks already total 120 minutes. The intake acknowledges that FT11 scheduling is unresolved, so the current shared learner instruction states an unapproved Fast pacing decision.

The module note promises a recap, but no loading objective or manifest rule makes the Fast path self-contained, so a Fast learner is formally asked to use psycopg before the prerequisite is taught.

The objectives span comprehensions, exception handling, generators, Pydantic rejection handling, deduplication, and pytest fixtures/parametrization, so the declared 30-minute coding fit cannot yet be evaluated or authored consistently.

All actual rows are mapped, so this is an evidence-count error rather than a syllabus omission.
